## Purpose

- Practice writing `lavaan()` model syntax for LVPA models (measurement model **plus** structural paths)

Each scenario below gives you a research question and some background.

In this rlab, for each scenario:

1. Decide which latent variables there are, and which indicators measure each one.
2. Decide which latent variables are **exogenous** and which are **endogenous**, and which way the structural paths go.
3. Write the model in lavaan syntax (just the model, we won't fit it in this class).
  - only change the Model, nothing else.
4. Run the `semPaths()` code to check that the diagram matches the model you intended.
5. Refer to lecture slides for relevant symbols.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
These are **fictional scenarios**, and the data are placeholders. Because we never fit the models, the numbers do not matter, only the structure.
:::

## Setup

```{r}
#| message: false
#| code-fold: false
library(lavaan)
library(semPlot)

# Placeholder data: random numbers with the right column names.
# lavaan() needs *some* data to build the model object; since we use
# do.fit = FALSE, the values are never used.
make_dat <- function(vars, n = 200) {
  as.data.frame(setNames(replicate(length(vars), rnorm(n), simplify = FALSE), vars))
}
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
```{r}
#| include: false
# Teacher-only: one helper that draws the answer diagram, so each scenario
# below only has to supply its model. Stripped from the student .qmd download.
answer_diagram <- function(model, vars) {
  fit0 <- lavaan(model, data = make_dat(vars), do.fit = FALSE)
  semPaths(fit0, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel",
           layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0,
           sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4)
}
```
:::

# Scenario 1

**Research question.** Does a **growth mindset** predict students' **engagement in math**?

**Background.**

- A district surveyed 8th graders with four Likert items about how they think about ability and three items about their experience in math class (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree).
- Researchers believe the four mindset items are driven by one construct, growth mindset, and the three engagement items by another, math engagement.
- Growth mindset is expected to **affect** math engagement. Nothing in the model explains growth mindset.
- Each item also has its own unique influences (wording, mood on the day, etc.).
- **Scaling:** set the scale of each latent variable by fixing its **first loading to 1**.

| Variable | Item |
|----------|------|
| `develop`  | "My intelligence can be developed"        |
| `workhard` | "Working hard makes me smarter"           |
| `hardsubj` | "I can get better even at hard subjects"  |
| `mistakes` | "Mistakes help me learn"                  |
| `enjoy`    | "I enjoy math class"                      |
| `focus`    | "I stay focused during math"              |
| `persist`  | "I keep trying when math gets hard"       |

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
vars1 <- c("develop", "workhard", "hardsubj", "mistakes", "enjoy", "focus", "persist")

model1 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit1 <- lavaan(model1, data = make_dat(vars1), do.fit = FALSE)

semPaths(fit1, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel",
         layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0,
         sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4)
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| code-fold: false
vars1 <- c("develop", "workhard", "hardsubj", "mistakes", "enjoy", "focus", "persist")
model1 <- "
  mindset =~ 1*develop + workhard + hardsubj + mistakes
  engage  =~ 1*enjoy + focus + persist
  engage  ~ mindset
  mindset ~~ mindset
  engage  ~~ engage
  develop ~~ develop
  workhard ~~ workhard
  hardsubj ~~ hardsubj
  mistakes ~~ mistakes
  enjoy ~~ enjoy
  focus ~~ focus
  persist ~~ persist
"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center
answer_diagram(model1, vars1)
```
:::
:::

# Scenario 2

**Research question.** Does **second-language (L2) anxiety** lower **L2 proficiency**?

**Background.**

- Adult learners of English completed three anxiety scales and took a proficiency test with three sections (scores in points).
- The anxiety scales are expected to reflect one construct, L2 anxiety. The three test sections are expected to reflect another, L2 proficiency.
- Theory says anxiety **affects** proficiency. Nothing in the model explains anxiety.
- **Scaling:** set the scale of **L2 anxiety** by fixing its **variance to 1** (so all of its loadings are free). Set the scale of **L2 proficiency** by fixing its **first loading to 1**.

| Variable | Item |
|----------|------|
| `classroom` | classroom anxiety scale   |
| `speaking`  | speaking anxiety scale    |
| `testanx`   | test anxiety scale        |
| `listening` | listening section score   |
| `reading`   | reading section score     |
| `writing`   | writing section score     |

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
vars2 <- c("classroom", "speaking", "testanx", "listening", "reading", "writing")

model2 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit2 <- lavaan(model2, data = make_dat(vars2), do.fit = FALSE)

semPaths(fit2, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel",
         layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0,
         sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4)
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| code-fold: false
vars2 <- c("classroom", "speaking", "testanx", "listening", "reading", "writing")
model2 <- "
  anx  =~ NA*classroom + speaking + testanx
  prof =~ 1*listening + reading + writing
  prof ~ anx
  anx  ~~ 1*anx
  prof ~~ prof
  classroom ~~ classroom
  speaking ~~ speaking
  testanx ~~ testanx
  listening ~~ listening
  reading ~~ reading
  writing ~~ writing
"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center
answer_diagram(model2, vars2)
```
:::
:::

# Scenario 3

**Research question.** Does **academic motivation** predict students' **GPA**?

**Background.**

- High school students completed three motivation scales (scores in points). Their GPA was taken from school records.
- The motivation scales are expected to reflect one construct, academic motivation.
- GPA is a **single measured variable**, not a latent variable. It is **not** measured by multiple indicators.
- Motivation is expected to **affect** GPA. Nothing in the model explains motivation.
- Students' grade level was also collected but is not part of this research question.
- **Scaling:** set the scale of motivation by fixing its **first loading to 1**.

| Variable | Item |
|----------|------|
| `effort`   | effort scale                |
| `homework` | homework completion scale   |
| `attend`   | attendance scale            |
| `gpa`      | grade point average         |
| `grade`    | grade level (9-12)          |

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
vars3 <- c("effort", "homework", "attend", "gpa", "grade")

model3 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit3 <- lavaan(model3, data = make_dat(vars3), do.fit = FALSE)

semPaths(fit3, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel",
         layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0,
         sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4)
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| code-fold: false
vars3 <- c("effort", "homework", "attend", "gpa", "grade")
model3 <- "
  # `grade` is not part of this research question, so it is left out
  motiv =~ 1*effort + homework + attend
  gpa   ~ motiv
  motiv ~~ motiv
  gpa   ~~ gpa
  effort ~~ effort
  homework ~~ homework
  attend ~~ attend
"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center
answer_diagram(model3, vars3)
```
:::
:::

# Scenario 4

**Research question.** How do customers' **trust in a brand**, their **perceived product quality**, and their **purchase intention** affect one another?

**Background.**

- An online survey of shoppers asked a set of questions on 7-point agreement scales.
- Theory says trust in the brand affects perceived quality, and perceived quality affects purchase intention. Trust is also expected to affect purchase intention **directly**, beyond its effect through quality.
- Nothing in the model explains trust.
- Two of the purchase-intention items were worded almost identically ("I plan to buy" and "I intend to buy"), so the researchers expect their unique parts (residuals) to **covary** beyond what purchase intention explains.
- **Scaling:** set the scale of **trust** by fixing its **variance to 1** (so all of its loadings are free). Set the scale of the other two latent variables by fixing their **first loadings to 1**.

| Variable | Item |
|----------|------|
| `reliable`   | "The product is reliable"              |
| `buysoon`    | "I will buy this product soon"         |
| `trustbrand` | "I trust this brand"                   |
| `plantobuy`  | "I plan to buy this product"           |
| `promises`   | "This brand keeps its promises"        |
| `lasts`      | "The product lasts a long time"        |
| `intendbuy`  | "I intend to buy this product"         |
| `honest`     | "This brand is honest with customers"  |
| `wellmade`   | "The product is well made"             |
| `shopfreq`   | "I shop online at least once a week"   |

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# YOUR TURN
vars4 <- c("reliable", "buysoon", "trustbrand", "plantobuy", "promises",
           "lasts", "intendbuy", "shopfreq", "honest", "wellmade")

model4 <- "
  # ...your model here...
"
fit4 <- lavaan(model4, data = make_dat(vars4), do.fit = FALSE)

semPaths(fit4, what = "path", whatLabels = "name", style = "lisrel",
         layout = "tree", rotation = 2, residuals = TRUE, nCharNodes = 0,
         sizeMan = 8, sizeMan2 = 4)
```

::: {.content-visible when-profile="teacher"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: code (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| code-fold: false
vars4 <- c("reliable", "buysoon", "trustbrand", "plantobuy", "promises",
           "lasts", "intendbuy", "shopfreq", "honest", "wellmade")
model4 <- "
  # `shopfreq` measures none of the three constructs, so it is left out
  trust  =~ NA*trustbrand + promises + honest
  qual   =~ 1*wellmade + reliable + lasts
  intent =~ 1*buysoon + plantobuy + intendbuy
  qual   ~ trust
  intent ~ qual + trust
  trust  ~~ 1*trust
  qual   ~~ qual
  intent ~~ intent
  trustbrand ~~ trustbrand
  promises ~~ promises
  honest ~~ honest
  wellmade ~~ wellmade
  reliable ~~ reliable
  lasts ~~ lasts
  buysoon ~~ buysoon
  plantobuy ~~ plantobuy
  intendbuy ~~ intendbuy
  plantobuy ~~ intendbuy
"
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Model answer: diagram (teacher)"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-align: center
answer_diagram(model4, vars4)
```
:::
:::
